chapter.title: Weaving Mats
chapter.tagline: Exploring tessellations, symmetry, and repeating geometric motifs in traditional woven crafts
chapter.overview: Inspired by bamboo weavers and traditional floor mats, students investigate how geometric shapes tile together without leaving gaps or overlaps. They study translational, rotational, and reflective symmetry in textile borders and floor patterns.

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look closely at this bamboo mat: strips go over two and under two in a steady rhythm, creating diagonal steps and diamonds!

concept.heading: Periodic Rhythms in Weaving
concept.keyRule: Systematic interlacing of warp and weft threads generates predictable mathematical patterns and symmetries.

sections.title: Floor Tessellations: Tiling Without Gaps
sections.subtitle: Which polygons fit together perfectly to tile a plane?

storyNarrative.dialogue: Hexagons and squares tile together with zero gaps, but regular pentagons leave awkward gaps! Why do some shapes tile while others cannot?

concept.heading: Tessellation Angle Rule
concept.keyRule: For regular polygons to tessellate around a vertex, the sum of their interior angles meeting at that vertex must equal exactly 360°.

sections.title: Symmetry Grids & Repeating Motifs
sections.subtitle: Designing symmetrical borders on square grids

storyNarrative.dialogue: If I draw a motif on the top left of my grid and reflect it across both vertical and horizontal center lines, a gorgeous royal mat emerges!

concept.heading: Two-Fold Reflectional Symmetry
concept.keyRule: Reflecting a motif across orthogonal axes produces 4-fold symmetric designs found in traditional rugs and rangolis.
